tool_args.rationale: All paid observations are positive and lie below H=0.46, where the candidate mechanisms can agree. The slow-horizon probe tests whether the response reverses near H=20 and constrains the slow component where the forecast is needed.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the dual-exponential reversal model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Five observations at H=0.28–0.45 do not constrain the slow amplitude and time constant well enough to forecast at H=20.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the monotone Arrhenius model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Positive short-horizon responses do not distinguish this model from one that reverses later.
It costs less but does not directly target the long-horizon behavior responsible for the forecast uncertainty.
At the same cost, prefer measuring near the forecast horizon over increasing temporal resolution.
